misconceptions.description: Treating a small formative session as proof of a population-level finding
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses words like proved, confirmed, or always after testing a handful of users
misconceptions.feedback: Scale the claim to the sample. A few sessions surface candidate problems; reserve proof language for verified, larger evidence.

misconceptions.description: Reporting a negative comment or preference as if it were an observed task failure
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports users 'hate' or 'failed' when the data shows a comment but no completion failure
misconceptions.feedback: Separate what participants said from what they did. Report comments and task outcomes as distinct evidence.

misconceptions.description: Letting an AI tool's confidence wording set the strength of a usability finding
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts an AI 'high confidence' label as the finding without checking counts or outcomes
misconceptions.feedback: Set claim strength from observed counts and task outcomes, not from an AI tool's asserted confidence.

misconceptions.description: Generalizing one participant's suggestion into a population need and a large decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'users want X' from a single comment and scales a major build on it
misconceptions.feedback: Attribute the suggestion to the one participant and verify demand before escalating it into a major decision.
